items.heading: Disrupting Democracy: Graphic Images
items.excerpt: Graphic Images uses data-driven visual storytelling to examine the forces reshaping democracy around the world. Drawing on data from the Bertelsmann Transformation Index (BTI), the project explores how technological, political, economic, and social changes, including polarization and information disruption, are influencing democratic systems and shaping their future.

items.heading: How to Fix Democracy
items.subheading: Interviews on democracy's past, present and future
items.excerpt:
Since its origins, democracy has been a work in progress; today, many question its resilience.
The Bertelsmann Foundation and Humanity in Action have teamed up with Andrew Keen, author of How to Fix the Future, to launch this video and podcast series exploring practical responses to the threats facing democracies around the world.
items.description:
How to Fix Democracy explores the challenges facing democratic systems and the ideas, innovations, and solutions that can strengthen them. Through conversations with experts, practitioners, and leaders from around the world, the podcast examines how societies can rebuild trust, address polarization, and ensure democracy remains resilient in a changing world.

Hosted by author and writer Andrew Keen, How to Fix Democracy brings together leading thinkers, writers, politicians, technologists, and business leaders to explore the challenges facing democracy and examine ideas for its renewal.

Launched in 2019, the podcast explores democracy's origins, evolution, successes, and shortcomings in the 21st century. Through in-depth conversations, the series examines how democratic institutions and societies can respond to today's challenges and adapt for the future.
items.microsite_cta: The complete experience lives on the How to Fix Democracy microsite.

items.heading: 100 Questions
items.excerpt: Recent technological advances are changing the way we do business, govern, and interact with each other. This shift is causing some concern over the future of work as technological innovations such as artificial intelligence and automation affect work. This challenge requires all members of the society to take action that will ensure technology creates a future that works and benefits everyone.

items.heading: Summer Enrichment Series
items.excerpt: The Summer Enrichment Series (SES) is a Bertelsmann Foundation program was launched in 2022. Each summer, the SES brings together a diverse group of graduate students and young professionals who have a strong interest in the transatlantic relationship.  Monthly roundtable events in June, July, and August have a thematic focus corresponding with relevant geopolitical events shaping the transatlantic alliance.
items.description:
Launched in 2022, the Summer Enrichment Series (SES) is a Bertelsmann Foundation program that brings together students and young professionals with a strong interest in the transatlantic relationship. Through monthly roundtable discussions in June, July, and August, participants engage with experts and peers on timely issues shaping the transatlantic partnership and exploring the geopolitical developments influencing the alliance.

The series provides an opportunity for the next generation of leaders to exchange perspectives, expand their networks, and deepen their understanding of the challenges and opportunities facing the United States and Europe.

items.excerpt: RANGE (Rethinking Assumptions in a New Geostrategic Environment) is a crowdsourced forecasting program focused on geopolitics and the transatlantic relationship.

items.heading: Bridging the Atlantic
items.excerpt:
*Bridging the Atlantic* is a 6-part miniseries, created with [Are We Europe](https://www.areweeurope.com/), that will take stock of transatlantic relations today and examine it beyond the usual touchstones. After a tumultuous four years with the Trump administration, many following the transatlantic relationship are eager to understand how the transatlantic relationship can bounce back and become more resilient in the future. But a reset is perhaps not the right goal. 

In the 21st century, people on both sides of the Atlantic are no longer satisfied with “back to normal” and want more. Through interviews with experts on various aspects of the transatlantic relationship, this podcast will pit our understanding of transatlantic relations over the last several years against ideas from people re-imagining what the transatlantic relationship can and should be. The outcome, we hope, is a clearer sense of the alliance that shapes our lives in visible and invisible ways.

items.heading: City Solutions Series
items.excerpt:
The commitment to liberal democracy is a core value of the transatlantic community. And while democracy has always faced external threats, a second front has emerged in recent years, challenging its fundamental principles from within. On every continent, local and national governments are experimenting with new methods of tackling the threats to public confidence and democratic governance by addressing a range of common challenges. The drivers of democratic backsliding are now clear, so this project focuses on uncovering solutions, then amplifies these best practices for a transatlantic audience searching for innovative approaches to reverse democratic decline.

It is often said that local government serves as a laboratory of democracy where new ideas and civic innovation transform the public space. It is also local government and civic leaders who offer the stoutest resistance when democracy is under attack. The objective of this joint project created by the Bertelsmann Foundation and the cities program at the German Marshall Fund is to surface those local innovations in democratic practice, and elevate them to national and international stakeholders who are constantly in search of positive evolutions to strengthen institutions, to make democracy more inclusive, and to stem the tide of authoritarianism. The hybrid approach to our research will make our deliverables accessible to policymakers and the public, with the goal of reshaping democracy around the globe by educating stakeholders at both ends of the influence spectrum.
items.description: The City Solutions Series explores how local governments and communities are developing innovative approaches to strengthen democratic governance and rebuild public trust. Through research and documentary storytelling, the project highlights practical solutions to common democratic challenges and shares lessons from transatlantic communities including Minneapolis (Minnesota), Lexington (Kentucky), Oklahoma City (Oklahoma), Barcelona (Spain), Athens (Greece) and Vienna (Austria).

items.heading: Leadership in Action
items.excerpt:
In its third season, Leadership in Action explores the strategies of skilled negotiators and practitioners as they tackle some of the world’s most intractable challenges. The first episode features Jan Eliasson, former Swedish Foreign Minister and Deputy Secretary-General of the United Nations, reflecting on pivotal moments in his career spent resolving global conflicts. The second episode highlights Ugandan opposition leader Bobi Wine, who takes us on a harrowing journey from repression to mobilizing a nation in the fight for democracy. The third episode focuses on Tzipi Livni, former Israeli Foreign Minister, filmed prior to the Hamas terror attack on October 7, 2023, and the ongoing conflict. It explores her role as Israel's chief negotiator during peace talks with the Palestinian Authority in the final rounds of negotiations in the 2000s.

Leadership in Action is part of an ongoing collaboration between the Bertelsmann Foundation and the Aspen Institute’s Aspen Ministers Forum.
items.description:
Now in its fifth season, Leadership in Action explores the experiences, strategies, and lessons of leaders who have navigated some of the world's most complex challenges. Through in-depth conversations with diplomats, policymakers, and practitioners, the series examines how leadership, negotiation, and resilience shape responses to conflict, political change, and global crises.

Previous episodes have featured Jan Eliasson, former Swedish Foreign Minister and Deputy Secretary-General of the United Nations, reflecting on his decades of diplomatic efforts to resolve international conflicts; Ugandan opposition leader Bobi Wine, discussing his journey from political repression to mobilizing a movement for democracy; and Tzipi Livni, former Israeli Foreign Minister, sharing insights from her role as Israel's chief negotiator during peace talks with the Palestinian Authority in the 2000s.

Produced in ongoing collaboration with the Aspen Ministers Forum of the Aspen Institute, Leadership in Action brings together the perspectives of experienced leaders and practitioners to highlight the lessons of diplomacy, negotiation, and leadership in addressing today's global challenges.

items.heading: The Bertelsmann Foundation Fellowship
items.excerpt: The Bertelsmann Foundation Fellowship (BFF), formerly known as the Congressional European Parliamentary Initiative (CEPI), offers a unique transatlantic hybrid experience spanning five months, designed to foster connections, knowledge transfer, and learning. Each year, the fellowship delves into global challenges confronting the transatlantic alliance. Commencing with an in-person trip to Washington, D.C., fellows then embark on a three-month virtual program, meeting weekly with experts relevant to the year's theme. The fellowship culminates with a visit to Brussels facilitating further in-person engagement. At the program's conclusion, fellows collaborate on a final publication presenting concrete policy recommendations pertaining to the chosen topic, released as an outcome of the BFF initiative. Fellows then also become a part of a larger, active Alumni network- finding opportunities to engage with the Bertelsmann Foundation Fellowship beyond their fellowship year.
items.description:
Building on the legacy of the Congressional European Parliamentary Initiative (CEPI), the Bertelsmann Foundation Fellowship (BFF) is an eight-month hybrid transatlantic fellowship program that connects emerging leaders from North America and Europe to exchange perspectives, build lasting networks, and deepen their understanding of the issues shaping the transatlantic relationship.

Each year, fellows explore a defining global challenge through a combination of virtual discussions with experts, policymakers, and thought leaders, as well as in-person engagements that foster dialogue, collaboration, and relationship-building across the Atlantic and beyond. The program culminates in a collaborative writing project that captures fellows' perspectives and insights on the year's theme.

Following the program, fellows become part of a growing transatlantic alumni network, with continued opportunities to engage with the Bertelsmann Foundation, fellow participants, and future cohorts.

items.heading: Transponder Magazine
items.excerpt:
The Transponder is the Bertelsmann Foundation’s biannual publication focusing on issues that impact the transatlantic relationship. The magazine features short-form and long-form articles, interviews, infographics and photo essays that explore topics related to democracy, technology, and geopolitics through a transatlantic lens. 

Want to receive Transponder updates and future issues? [Subscribe here.](https://mailchi.mp/bfna.org/transponder-sign-up)

items.heading: Wisdom of the Crowd
items.subheading: A podcast miniseries by the Bertelsmann Foundation and Are We Europe
items.excerpt:
Welcome to “Wisdom of the Crowd”, a podcast miniseries that explores the future of transatlantic relations. From democracy and geopolitics to climate change and technology, we take a closer look at the most pressing issues impacting the transatlantic alliance by interviewing top experts and using a strategy of crowd-sourced forecasting. We don’t just rely on experts and policy makers; we listen to a crowd of forecasters, and YOU, to determine the outcome of future events. We call that “the wisdom of the crowd”. Wisdom of the Crowd is produced by the Bertelsmann Foundation, Are We Europe, and Awe Studio. Sound design is done by Stefano Montali and the podcast artwork is by Tamara Tasić. This series is hosted by Rylie Munn.

Listen wherever you get your podcasts: [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/show/3FZNWMZJIEclBonA0V6wLx?si=68c852b2fb7d42c7), [Apple Music](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/wisdom-of-the-crowd/id1674421315), [Google Podcasts](https://podcasts.google.com/feed/aHR0cHM6Ly9mZWVkcy5zaW1wbGVjYXN0LmNvbS9SMmxVYmwyaA?sa=X&ved=0CAMQ4aUDahcKEwjQtIi4sbv9AhUAAAAAHQAAAAAQBg), and more.

Sign up to become a forecaster on [RANGE](https://www.rangeforecasting.org/) and join the conversation!

items.heading: Critical Minerals: Securing the Resources of the Future
items.excerpt: The Critical Minerals initiative examines how the global race for essential resources such as lithium, nickel, and cobalt is reshaping energy, technology, and geopolitics. Through documentary films, research, and public dialogue, the project explores challenges and opportunities surrounding supply chains, responsible resource development, and international cooperation.

items.heading: Election Analysis
items.excerpt: The Election Analysis initiative examines major elections in the United States and Europe, as well as the issues and institutions shaping electoral processes. Through analysis, explanatory videos, podcasts, expert interviews, and briefing discussions, the project provides insights into campaigns, voting trends, and election-related debates while fostering a deeper understanding of political developments across the Atlantic.

items.heading: BFNA Documentaries
items.excerpt: BFNA Documentaries brings the Foundation’s research and reporting to life on screen — candid, honest films that let viewers draw their own conclusions.
items.description:
BFNA Documentaries brings the Foundation’s research and reporting to life on screen. Believing in the power of film to tell the critical stories of our complicated times, its films present candid, honest perspectives without projecting an agenda, allowing viewers to draw their own conclusions.

The catalog spans more than 35 films, including the series Democracy in Cities, People in Evidence, and Leadership in Action, with works screened and recognized at festivals internationally.
